thread:
alex: Heads-up — I ran the new apples-to-apples harness comparing synthetic spikes vs replay for the continuous-batching patch. Seeing a weird latency cliff when kernel_selector switches to the fused-attn path at ~512 tokens. p95 jumps ~2.5x for a subset of tenants.

morgan: Ugh. Is that correlated with batch growth or KV cache hit-rate?

alex: Initial signal looks like batch size + kv hit interplay. When batch grows above ~16 and the active KV cache hit < 0.6, we drop into that kernel path and per-token throughput decreases. I attached a short config I used.

morgan: can you paste the harness command and config? quick glance will help reproduce.

alex: Sure — run: 
```
./harness/replay_runner --trace --pin-kernel=fused-attn-v2 --batch-cap=32 --max-wait-ms=8 --replay=tenant_replay_2026.json
```
and the bench snippet: 
```json
{
  "batch_cap": 32,
  "max_wait_ms": 8,
  "kernel_selector": "auto",
  "kv_cache_prefetch": true
}
```
(note: I pinned kernel for the initial repro then re-ran with auto)

sam: I profiled the hot path. When fused-attn-v2 is selected, we see a bigger L2 thrash for sequences > 480; the kernel's scratch memory alloc pattern causes a stall on memcpy for certain alignment patterns. Flame graph shows a memcpy spike. Also noticed GC-like small allocations from the allocator during KV fallback.

priya: Interesting. So might be two levers: prevent kernel swap by capping batch growth OR nudge kernel selector to prefer chunked-attn for mid-length sequences. Which one is easier to A/B?

alex: For apples-to-apples I'd prefer to keep kernel fixed across comparisons and vary batching heuristics only. That isolates batching/kv effects.

perf-bot: [deploy-bench] replay harness scheduled: run-id=rb-2026-03-10-17, note=isolated-kernel-vs-batching

morgan: Agreed with alex. Proposal: three-phase experiment per tenant slice: (1) pin kernel to fused-attn-v2, sweep batch_cap {8,16,24,32} and max_wait_ms {2,8,20}, (2) repeat with kernel pinned to chunked-attn, (3) auto selector but with kv_prefetch toggled. Collect p50/p95/p99, kv-hit, batch-size-dist, queue-delay-dist, and tenant-weighted-p99.

sam: Add one more metric: "latency cliff frequency" — count of requests where latency >= 2x median within same 1-min window. That captures microbursts that hurt SLAs.

priya: For fairness testing, we should run multi-tenant mixes: heavy (70% qps) + light tenants. Measure relative p95 uplift on light tenants when heavy ones trigger fused-attn. If fused-attn introduces long per-token stalls, it can monopolize the GPU and starve other queues. Use tenant-isolation tag in the harness to simulate.

alex: Good call. Also add a variant with small max_wait_ms but larger batch_cap (e.g., max_wait_ms=2, batch_cap=48) to see if artificially forcing big batches quickly causes more cliffing versus slow ramp (max_wait_ms=20, batch_cap=32).

morgan: Timeline? I can spin the job cluster today for slices 1-2. sam can attach perf traces, priya will own fairness analysis.

sam: I'll instrument extra histograms and upload flamegraphs to the bench artifacts bucket. If memcpy is the issue we can try an allocator tweak or a kernel patch.

priya: I'll prepare the tenant mixes and the post-processing notebook for weighted-p99 and cliff-frequency plots. We should set an alert if tenant-weighted-p99 increases >10% compared to baseline.

alex: Action items in thread: 1) morgan: launch sweep (today), 2) sam: perf traces + memcpy verification, 3) priya: fairness notebook + alert rule proposal. I'll collate results and we can pick mitigation (selector tweak vs allocator vs batch heuristic) next week.
